title: The Alex panel
summary: The right-hand panel is Alex, the one assistant, with one row of tabs: Co-engineer, Ask, Agent, Plan and E1 Guide; its badge says Built-in or names the model, and the panel can be hidden and shown from the left rail.
roles: Everyone

title: Alex: let the built-in engineering co-worker help
summary: Alex reads your 2D space as you work and lists warnings, questions and suggestions, locally, with no language model.
roles: Anyone who may edit the 2D space

title: Why “Alex”? What stays local
summary: A note in Alex (Co-engineer) explains the name and that Alex sends nothing outside.
roles: Everyone

training.topic: Why Alex is a local AI

title: E1 Guide: Alex shows you how, where you are
summary: Alex's trainer mode offers lessons for the place you are in and guides you through them with bubbles on the real buttons, each linked to this guide; a bubble whose button is not on screen shows the way to it, and the last bubble says what to learn next.
roles: Everyone; nothing is recorded about who took a lesson

training.topic: Learning E1 with the E1 Guide

title: Whole jobs, step by step: the E1 Guide's paths
summary: A path takes you through a whole job, such as drawing your first P&ID or issuing a drawing for review, lesson after lesson in the order the work is done.
roles: Everyone

training.topic: Learning E1 with the E1 Guide

title: What is this? Ask E1 about any button
summary: Click What is this? in the E1 Guide, or press Shift+F1, then click any button or field: instead of using it, E1 shows what it does and the lessons that teach it.
roles: Everyone

training.topic: Learning E1 with the E1 Guide

title: Show me how: the idea first, then each step
summary: On the pages that do special work, Show me how opens one page on how the thing works, with a picture, its ideas and the work from start to finish; Show me step by step then shows each step on the screen.
roles: Everyone

training.topic: Learning E1 with the E1 Guide

title: Choose Alex's skill and level
summary: The skill decides which engineer reads the drawing; the level decides how much Alex tells you.
roles: Everyone

title: Read and act on Alex's cards
summary: Each finding is a card with why, where, and a fix, an answer field or a way to set it aside.
roles: Reading: everyone; Apply and Save need edit rights

title: Read Alex's simulation results
summary: When Alex has simulated the open 2D space, its results appear as Simulation results cards with the method, the inputs, the assumptions and the result tables.
roles: Everyone

title: Alex's marks on the drawing
summary: Warnings and questions are marked on the drawing and linked both ways to their cards; the marks can be hidden.
roles: Everyone

title: Filter Alex's findings
summary: The count chips filter the cards and marks by kind, or to the selected symbol.
roles: Everyone

title: Not applicable: hide a finding, or propose it to the company
summary: Hide a finding on this 2D space, or propose that Alex never raises it at your company.
roles: Hiding: everyone; proposing: members who may propose waivers; accepting: convention approvers

training.topic: When a finding does not apply

title: Suggestions while you draw: Apply or Reject
summary: While Alex is on, Alex offers what usually comes next, such as the valves around a new pump, as ghost symbols and an After your change card to apply or reject.
roles: Anyone who may edit the 2D space

title: Ask Alex about a card in your own words
summary: Opens Alex's Ask tab with an Alex finding as a ready-written question that you can edit before sending.
roles: Everyone who may use Alex's AI help

title: Teach Alex your company's conventions (Alex knowledge)
summary: Upload your standards; Alex proposes the rules it finds, and once accepted checks every drawing against them.
roles: Engineering standards owner, Library administrator or owner

title: Team memory: what is usual at your company
summary: Alex learns the usual values from your projects and suggests them on new lines.
roles: Turning it on needs the permission to approve conventions

title: Pipe class checks
summary: With your pipe classes loaded, Alex checks each line's pressure, temperature, class and sour service against them.
roles: As for Alex knowledge

title: Export the instrument index from the drawing
summary: Alex writes the instrument index, I/O list, cause and effect and motor list of a 2D space into one Excel workbook.
roles: Automation or Plant engineer skill

title: Import a heat and material balance
summary: Brings a simulator's stream table into the line list, matched to lines and checked by you.
roles: Process or Plant engineer skill and permission to write values

training.topic: Importing a heat and material balance

title: Ask, Agent and Plan: talk with Alex
summary: In Alex's tabs Ask, Agent and Plan, Alex answers in your own words with a language model and, in Agent, changes the project with review and undo; Co-engineer and E1 Guide send nothing.
roles: Everyone in an installation with an AI model; changes need an Editor license and a project role that may edit

training.topic: Asking Alex in your own words

title: Ask, Agent and Plan: what each may do
summary: Alex's tabs: Ask only answers, Agent edits the project, and Plan proposes a change that waits for Apply.
roles: Everyone who may use Alex's AI help

title: Review changes first: Apply or Discard
summary: Alex works on a draft and nothing is stored until you click Apply.
roles: Anyone who may let Alex edit with its AI help

title: Protect the arrangement
summary: Alex may add to the drawing but does not move, resize or reroute what is already drawn.
roles: Anyone who may let Alex edit with its AI help

title: Undo everything a reply changed
summary: One click on a reply takes back its whole change.
roles: Editor license and a project role that may edit, in every project the change touched

title: What is always held for review
summary: Large deletions and some commands always wait for Apply, even with Review changes first off.
roles: Everyone who lets Alex edit with its AI help

training.topic: Safety limits on Alex's AI help

title: Attach files to a message
summary: Give Alex a list, a specification or a screenshot; E1 reads the text and sends it with your message.
roles: Everyone who may use Alex's AI help

title: Voice input
summary: Speak instead of typing; the text lands in the text box for you to edit and send.
roles: Everyone who may use Alex's AI help

title: Which model: the model under Ask, Agent and Plan
summary: The model under Alex's Ask, Agent and Plan, and where messages go; Editors outside a trial may pick a premium model.
roles: Everyone sees it; premium models need an Editor license outside a trial

title: Choose the installation's model (operators)
summary: The installation's operators choose the model Alex gets help from for everyone, in Configuration → Alex’s AI help.
roles: Installation operators (E1_OPERATORS)

training.topic: Choosing the model for Alex's AI help

title: Engineering patterns: pump trains, instrument taps, motor feeders
summary: Alex, with its AI help, draws three common designs correctly and checks and repairs what it drew.
roles: Anyone who may edit the 2D space

title: Alex's review behind the answer
summary: Before judging a design, Alex's own review of the sheet runs with your company's conventions, and the model's answer rests on it.
roles: Everyone who may use Alex's AI help

training.topic: Alex's review and the model together

title: Text in the project is data, not instructions
summary: Alex and its model never follow instructions written in names, notes, attributes or attached files.
roles: Everyone

title: Without a language model: Co-engineer, everything by hand
summary: With no AI model, Alex's AI help switched off or the credits used up, Alex works on its own and you do the rest by hand with the menus, toolbars and right-click menus.
roles: Everyone

title: Outside agents through MCP (administrators and developers)
summary: An outside AI agent can run E1's commands through the Model Context Protocol, recorded and undoable in History.
roles: Administrators and developers with access to the installation

title: Stored assistants
summary: Save what Alex did in one reply, or record what you do, as an assistant, and run it again on another selection without Alex: one change, one undo, or a preview first; repeat it for each selected object and skip a step when it is not needed. Share one with the project or the organization, and pin it on the left rail. An instruction assistant keeps what Alex should do, in your words.
roles: Saving needs Create assistants and running Run assistants (Engineer and above); each step also needs its own permission

title: Assistants from content packages, other assistants and the API
summary: Content packages bring assistants of their own, such as Plant's Describe the duty of pumps and Set design conditions, under From content packages; an assistant can run another assistant as one of its steps; and another system runs an assistant through the integration API.
roles: Running: Run stored assistants (Engineer and above) with each step's own permission

title: A script step in a stored assistant
summary: A step that calculates values from the assistant's parameters and earlier results, with the steps of a calculation rule, for the steps after it.
roles: Whoever may make assistants

title: Alex in your branch
summary: Alex, with its AI help, will make its changes in your own branch, and held changes will be temporary branches.
roles: To be decided

title: Queries from a sentence
summary: Ask Alex for “all pumps without a motor”: Alex turns the sentence into a query (query_from_sentence), runs it (run_query) and answers with the rows; the integration API offers the same.
roles: Any project role that may view the project
